transcript.text: LG GSXV91BSAE showing Er FF and the freezer is only about -8. There's a scraping noise and frost on the back wall inside. Help!

The 'Er FF' code on your LG fridge-freezer indicates a Freezer Fan fault, but combined with the scraping noise and frost build-up, this is almost certainly caused by a failed defrost system (likely the defrost heater or thermostat). When the defrost cycle fails, ice builds up over the evaporator coils behind that back wall. The fan blade then hits this ice blockage, causing the scraping sound and preventing cold air from circulating properly to your freezer. To confirm this is a temporary icing issue rather than a permanent motor failure, we need to clear the ice completely. Please switch the fridge off at the wall socket, move the food into cool bags with towels inside to catch melting water, and leave both doors open for 24 hours until every bit of ice has melted. Once it's dry, plug it back in. Does the scraping noise stop completely after this full manual defrost?

I can't leave it off for 24 hours, my freezer is full and I've nowhere to put the food. Could I do 6-8 hours overnight with the food wrapped in towels instead? Also the freezer is at -8 so I'm worried about the food.

Yes, a 6–8 hour overnight defrost is acceptable if you wrap the food in towels and place it in the coolest part of your kitchen (or a cool room) away from direct heat. Please switch the fridge off at the wall socket now, clear any ice you can safely reach without forcing it, and leave the doors open for that time. Tomorrow morning, check if the scraping noise is gone when you turn it back on.
Ok, I'll do the overnight defrost with the food wrapped in towels. Should I do anything about the frost on the back wall, or just leave it to melt? I won't take the back panel off though.

Just leave the frost to melt naturally; do not chip or scrape at it as you could puncture the cooling pipes. Since you aren't removing the back panel, ensure any water that runs down from the melting ice is caught with towels on the shelf below so it doesn't pool in the fridge section. Once the 6–8 hours are up and everything is dry, plug it back in and set the freezer to -18°C. Listen carefully: if the scraping noise is gone but you still hear a humming fan (or silence), leave it running for 24 hours. However, because the 'Er FF' code indicates an electrical fault in the defrost cycle, this will likely recur until the part causing the icing is replaced by a qualified engineer.
